item.title: AirLink 0.12.0-beta.3
item.description:
# AirLink 0.12.0 Beta 3
This beta corrects a misleading sender status after a connection is restored. A receiver waiting for approval now shows **Waiting for acceptance**, with the old network error cleared. The original offer and confirmed progress remain intact.
## Changes
- Persist a healthy waiting-for-acceptance status after reconnect; clear the obsolete connection error and speed sample. A failed save retains the previous state. Late responses cannot resume paused or cancelled transfers. - Avoid repeatedly writing unchanged waiting status. Hide unsupported Pause actions while an offer still awaits acceptance on macOS and Linux. - Document Linux firewall setup. Device discovery and pairing initiated from Linux can succeed while incoming file-transfer connections remain blocked. A real CachyOS/KDE investigation confirmed blocked TCP SYN packets at the default TLS port. A local-subnet-only rule restored a certificate-verified connection and delivered the previously queued offer to the receiver for approval.
## Downloads and updates
Choose the matching package: separate ARM64/x64 macOS DMGs, x64 Linux AppImage/DEB/RPM/Arch package, and x64/ARM64 Windows Setup. All eight packages use version **0.12.0-beta.3**, numeric OS build **16**, and the unchanged update public key. Existing 0.12 installations can use Check for Updates; native Linux packages stay under package-manager control. Automatic beta notices remain opt-in; installation requires a click.
On Arch, install the native package with:
```sh sudo pacman -U ./AirLink-0.12.0-beta.3-linux-x64.pkg.tar.zst ```
With an active firewall, permit the actual AirLink TLS port from the intended local network. The default is TCP 43871; the connection address shows the actual port if the default was busy. Keep the firewall enabled. See the Linux section in [README](https://github.com/lucaskleinsteuber/Airlink#linux) for a scoped UFW example. AirLink does not automatically change firewall/router policy.
**From Beta 1 or earlier:** first start migrates transfer metadata. Pairings, settings, confirmed checkpoints and received files remain preserved; older services cannot open the upgraded database. Beta 2 to Beta 3 uses the same storage format. Mac builds remain ad hoc signed and not notarized; Windows Setup builds are not Authenticode signed.
## Background verification and scope
- [Windows, macOS and Ubuntu suites passed](https://github.com/lucaskleinsteuber/Airlink/actions/runs/42834884019): Go race/vet, actual helper subprocesses, Swift/Core/web tests, both Mac/Windows architectures and Windows x64 silent installer acceptance. - [Six Linux package lifecycles passed](https://github.com/lucaskleinsteuber/Airlink/actions/runs/42834884131): Debian 12, Ubuntu 24.04, Arch, Fedora and both openSUSE variants, Qt Core with the installed helper, a genuinely newer synthetic successor, removal and preserved test data. - [Eight native application packages built](https://github.com/lucaskleinsteuber/Airlink/actions/runs/42835037598). Source/package privacy and retained-key signatures are verified before delivery. - New regression cases cover actual two-service recovery into recipient approval, continuation to matching final bytes, atomic status-save failure, restart and protection against stale results after pause/cancel.
No GUI/desktop-controlling tests are used. The physical investigation proves the firewall failure and restored trusted HTTPS/offer path. A complete new physical file/hash run is not claimed while the laptop's network connection is unavailable. Native updater interaction and the separate 100-GB device test remain manual evidence. This remains a beta; the [verification record](https://github.com/lucaskleinsteuber/Airlink/blob/main/docs/TESTING.md) separates background checks and physical acceptance. Beta 2 performance measurements retain their original version and scope; they are not new Beta 3 measurements.
